children: It was a major week for healthcare stocks, with 24 out of 60 companies reporting their results. Pharmaceutical heavyweights like Pfizer
posted broadly positive quarterly results throughout the week.
The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF
remained flat through the week even as the broader markets took a sharp plunge. In the year so far, the healthcare sector has risen more than 19% compared to a 7% rise in the S&P500 index.
Of the 24 firms that reported earnings this week, 23, or 95.8%, posted better-than-expected EPS, while one missed analysts’ estimate. Notably, 21 firms (87.5%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.
On the revenue front, four firms lagged analysts’ consensus while 83.3% or 20 firms posted top lines above expectations. Notably, 18 firms (75%) posted Y/Y revenue growth.
Below is a snapshot of the quarterly print of some major firms in the healthcare sector:

posted earnings marginally above Wall Street’s estimates at $0.87 per share on revenue of $16.58B, amid less demand for its COVID-19 products. However, the company raised its full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance to a range of $2.95 to $3.05 and hiked the revenue outlook to the range of $62B to $64B. Concurrently, Pfizer also appointed Cecile Guegan as its next chief financial officer and executive vice president.

posted a mixed performance for Q3 2026 on Thursday, falling short of consensus for revenue while beating earnings guidance as its generics sales for the quarter fell for the first time this year. EPS rose 6% YoY to $0.71 even as revenue remained flat at $3.7B, compared to the prior year. Citing the strong YTD performance, Viatris raised its full-year guidance ranges for revenue and adjusted EPS to $14.70B - $14.90B and $2.56 - $2.63, respectively.

shares bounced back after days of decline after the firm posted better-than-expected Q3 2026 results and lifted its full-year growth outlook, citing higher COVID vaccine sales in its overseas markets. It reported earnings of $0.38 per share for the quarter on revenue of $1.3B. Speaking about its cancer vaccine, Moderna said it remains on track to submit regulatory filings for intismeran autogene developed with Merck
and initiate its commercial launch, subject to regulatory approval.

Out of the pharma companies that reported earnings this week, three were biotechnology firms, and three were pharmaceutical companies. Seven of those belonged to the health care equipment industry, and another seven to the health care providers & services industry, while four came from life sciences tools & services.
With the earnings season drawing to a close, only one major healthcare firm, Hims & Hers Health
, is due to report its results next week.

title: Earnings Scorecard: 96% healthcare firms post EPS wins this week
